# Research README: physics-informed orbital propagation and conjunction screening

**Research and manuscript preparation dossier — audited 20 September 2026**

This document explains the implemented project, its mathematics, data, experiments, saved results, and a defensible route to an IEEE or Springer manuscript. It is a research companion to [README.md](README.md). It does not certify publication readiness or acceptance. Scientific strength depends on novelty, fair experiments, independent validation, reproducibility, and the selected venue's review.

**Recommended working title:** *Physics-Informed Short-Time Orbital Propagation and SGP4 Residual Learning: A Reproducible Evaluation for Conjunction Screening.*

**Central finding:** a physics-trained local orbital flow map is implemented and evaluated; its catalog agreement and independent orbit accuracy are distinct measurements. A supervised SGP4 residual corrector reduces error on one held-out Sentinel-1D interval, but receives additional ESA calibration data. None of these experiments demonstrates operational collision prediction.

## 1. Research scope and claims

### 1.1 Three different scientific questions

| Question | Available experiment | What its measurements mean |
|---|---|---|
| Can an equation-trained network propagate real catalog initial states and reproduce SGP4 screening decisions? | Catalog SGP4/PINN comparison | Agreement with another model |
| How close are frozen SGP4 and PINN trajectories to an independent orbit estimate? | One-hour Sentinel-1D ESA comparison | Independent-reference regression error on one arc |
| Can earlier ESA residuals improve later SGP4 states through a neural correction? | Three-hour chronological three-model experiment | Retrospective calibration and extrapolation on one satellite |
| Can the system predict actual collisions and calibrated collision probabilities? | No suitable independent event/uncertainty dataset | Not established |

A conjunction is an approach within a chosen distance threshold. It is not a collision. A threshold classifier is not a calibrated probability estimator.

### 1.2 Defensible contribution candidates

Describe these as the project's implemented contributions; priority or novelty relative to the literature remains to be demonstrated.

1. A short-time neural orbital flow map with exact initial conditions, a Taylor trial solution, geometric features, and central-gravity/J2 residual training.
2. A common-input SGP4/PINN screening comparison with explicit negative-pair universes, exclusion audits, and one-to-one episode matching in the dedicated comparison pipeline.
3. A frame-aligned independent ESA benchmark that distinguishes model agreement from external-reference accuracy.
4. A separately identified supervised SGP4 residual correction with chronological training, validation and test intervals.
5. Replayable experiments retaining source snapshots, inputs, weights, histories, errors, timings, and verification records.

Do not claim a new SGP4 theory, a first-ever orbital PINN, a physics-constrained hybrid, proven exhaustive screening, a general speedup, or validated collision prevention.

### 1.3 Research questions suitable for a paper

- RQ1: How well does the learned local flow map generalize to held-out catalog objects?
- RQ2: How do its errors accumulate with forecast horizon?
- RQ3: How do orbital state disagreements alter conjunction flags and encounter times?
- RQ4: Does a calibrated residual model improve later independent-reference errors?
- RQ5: What information, runtime and physical-consistency tradeoffs accompany those results?

The present evidence partially answers these questions. Section 13 identifies missing experiments.

## 3. Data, provenance, units and frames

### 3.1 CelesTrak catalog

The implemented default groups are stations, cosmos-2251-debris, iridium-33-debris and fengyun-1c-debris. This selected catalog is not all tracked space objects.

The request uses GP JSON with OMM keywords. Fields include NORAD_CAT_ID, OBJECT_NAME, OBJECT_ID, EPOCH, MEAN_MOTION, ECCENTRICITY, INCLINATION, RA_OF_ASC_NODE, ARG_OF_PERICENTER, MEAN_ANOMALY and BSTAR. Original derivative fields and source records are retained. GP elements are SGP4-compatible mean elements; do not treat them as unmodified osculating Keplerian elements. See [CelesTrak GP documentation](https://celestrak.org/NORAD/documentation/gp-data-formats.php).

| Quantity | Convention |
|---|---|
| Mean motion | revolutions/day |
| Angular element fields | degrees |
| Eccentricity | dimensionless |
| BSTAR | SGP4 parameter in inverse Earth radii; not a measured object area or covariance |
| State position / velocity | km / km s^-1 |
| Position covariance | km^2 |
| Time offsets | seconds |
| Epoch / reported time | UTC |
| Propagated coordinate frame | TEME |
| GP initialization constants | WGS72 |

Duplicate catalog IDs are merged using the newest epoch while retaining SOURCE_GROUPS. Download time is not element epoch. Cached snapshots do not represent new independent observations. The implemented fetch cache lasts two hours; manifests retain original retrieval times.

Initializations and propagation failures are audited. Default screening excludes objects with any invalid state and objects with absolute epoch age exceeding 72 hours at the forecast start. Epoch age at encounter time can be larger. This age cutoff is a project setting, not an error bound.

Catalog IDs above the sgp4 wrapper's supported internal encoding are internally replaced by a neutral identifier, while the actual IDs remain in external records and arrays. Catalog IDs do not affect orbital dynamics.

Identical orbital-element signatures are grouped for splitting and unresolved shared-orbit pairs are excluded from conjunction classification. Grouping exact signatures reduces one source of leakage; it does not remove all statistical dependence within breakup families.

### 3.2 Independent ESA reference

The saved independent dataset is Sentinel-1D, NORAD 66315, using ESA AUX_RESORB orbit state vectors reconstructed from onboard GNSS. It is a restituted estimate, not final AUX_POEORB and not error-free physical truth. Product categories are documented by [Copernicus](https://sentiwiki.copernicus.eu/web/s1-processing).

Saved metadata from reference_inputs/sentinel_benchmark/source_manifest.json:

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| GP epoch | 2026-09-13T00:10:10.325280Z |
| First benchmark state | 2026-09-13T00:10:14.932121Z |
| ESA state count / native cadence | 1,271 / 10 seconds |
| Actual reference coverage | 00:10:04.932121Z–03:41:44.932121Z, 13 September 2026 |
| ESA creation time | 2026-09-13T04:11:24 |
| GP download | 2026-09-13T09:26:33.578269+00:00 |
| ESA download | 2026-09-13T09:26:34.608242+00:00 |
| Accepted quality | NOMINAL |
| Input header frame / units | EARTH_FIXED / m and m s^-1 |
| Experiment sampling | Exact native states every 60 seconds |

The first initial state is SGP4 evaluated at the first selected native reference timestamp, approximately 4.607 seconds after the GP epoch. It is not initialized from ESA.

The products were obtained after the evaluated interval. This is a retrospective benchmark, even though the element epoch precedes the evaluated timestamps. Historical real-time availability is unproven.

### 3.3 Position AND velocity transformation

The implementation interprets ESA Earth-fixed states as ITRS, with CPOD terrestrial-realization context recorded in the manifest, then transforms them to TEME through Astropy. It uses ESA UT1-minus-UTC and saved IERS finals2000A polar motion. Automatic Earth-orientation downloads are disabled.

Conceptually, for a time-dependent rotation Q(t):

$$
\mathbf r_{\rm TEME}=Q(t)\mathbf r_{\rm ITRS},\qquad
\mathbf v_{\rm TEME}=Q(t)\mathbf v_{\rm ITRS}+\dot Q(t)\mathbf r_{\rm ITRS}. \tag{1}
$$

This equation explains why rotating velocity as if it were position is wrong; the implementation delegates the complete coordinate transformation to Astropy. Its satellite-frame conventions are documented in [Astropy's satellite guide](https://docs.astropy.org/en/stable/coordinates/satellites.html).

Both transformed quantities are round-trip checked, with maximum absolute component differences required below 10^-7 km and 10^-7 km/s. A small round-trip error is numerical consistency, not an absolute geophysical accuracy guarantee. The one-hour benchmark used predicted IERS-A polar motion (status 2); reference and frame uncertainty remain.

## 4. Problem definition and notation

For object i, let its Cartesian state be x_i(t) = [r_i(t), v_i(t)] in R^6. All comparisons must use identical timestamps and frames.

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| mu | Earth gravitational parameter |
| R_E | Earth equatorial radius in the dynamics |
| J2 | Second zonal gravity coefficient |
| L, T, V | Characteristic length, time and velocity scales |
| tau | Dimensionless local step time |
| theta, phi | Standalone PINN / residual-corrector parameters |
| N, K, B | Number of objects, time intervals, collocation batch size |
| d_thr | Screening threshold, normally 5 km |
| t_CA, d_CA | Predicted closest-approach time and miss distance |
| C_i, R_H | Supplied covariance and combined hard-body radius |
| R,T,N axes | Radial, transverse and normal directions; context distinguishes the time scale T |

The two-body/J2 state problem is

$$
\frac{d\mathbf r}{dt}=\mathbf v,\qquad
\frac{d\mathbf v}{dt}=\mathbf a(\mathbf r),\qquad
\mathbf r(t_0)=\mathbf r_0,\;\mathbf v(t_0)=\mathbf v_0. \tag{2}
$$

The pair-screening target is

$$
t_{CA}=\arg\min_{t\in[t_0,t_1]}\|\mathbf r_i(t)-\mathbf r_j(t)\|,\quad
d_{CA}=\|\mathbf r_i(t_{CA})-\mathbf r_j(t_{CA})\|,\quad
y_{ij}=\mathbb 1[d_{CA}\le d_{\rm thr}]. \tag{3}
$$

Implementation reports one minimum per contiguous candidate episode; a pair can have multiple episodes. Thus the global-window pair label and episode count are different objects.

## 5. SGP4 baseline

SGP4 is the established GP-compatible analytical propagator used through the sgp4 package, initialized directly from OMM fields with WGS72:

$$
(\widehat{\mathbf r}(t),\widehat{\mathbf v}(t))
 ={\cal P}_{SGP4}(\text{GP mean elements},t;\mathrm{WGS72}). \tag{4}
$$

Its full secular, periodic, drag and regime-dependent equations are supplied by the library; this project does not reimplement them. Equation (4) is an interface definition, not a replacement two-body derivation. Cite the complete algorithm in [Vallado et al., Revisiting Spacetrack Report #3](https://celestrak.org/publications/AIAA/2006-6753/), and the exact library/version.

Why use it: compatibility with GP data, a standard reference, efficient vectorized propagation, and published numerical verification cases. It is neither an observation nor guaranteed ground truth.

The code uses split Julian dates to retain sub-day precision:

$$
JD(t)=JD_0+f_0+\Delta t/86400,
$$

with integer carry and a separate fractional-day argument. Invalid error codes and nonfinite outputs are excluded rather than converted into plausible-looking trajectories.

The built-in numerical check evaluates Vallado satellite 00005 at epoch, requiring position-vector discrepancy below 10^-6 km and velocity-vector discrepancy below 10^-8 km/s. This checks one implementation case, not observational forecast performance.

## 6. Standalone PINN mathematics

### 6.1 Governing acceleration

The physical acceleration in km/s^2 is

$$
\mathbf a(\mathbf r)=-\frac{\mu}{r^3}\mathbf r+
\frac{3J_2\mu R_E^2}{2r^5}
\begin{bmatrix}
x(5z^2/r^2-1)\\
y(5z^2/r^2-1)\\
z(5z^2/r^2-3)
\end{bmatrix},\qquad r=\|\mathbf r\|. \tag{5}
$$

Implementation constants: mu = 398600.8 km^3/s^2, R_E = 6378.135 km, J2 = 0.001082616.

Central gravity supplies dominant orbital attraction; J2 represents Earth's oblateness at low additional computational cost. This is a simplified model. Atmospheric drag, J3/J4, third-body forces, radiation pressure, maneuvers and time-dependent frame effects are absent. TEME is approximated as quasi-inertial.

### 6.2 Nondimensionalization

$$
L=7000\ {\rm km},\quad T=\sqrt{L^3/\mu},\quad V=L/T,\quad
\bar{\mathbf r}=\mathbf r/L,\quad\bar{\mathbf v}=\mathbf v/V,\quad\tau=\Delta t/T. \tag{6}
$$

The dimensionless central term is -r_bar/||r_bar||^3, while the J2 coefficient becomes (3/2)J2(R_E/L)^2. Scaling avoids directly combining thousands of kilometers, single-digit km/s and seconds in network inputs and losses.

### 6.3 Features and neural architecture

Let rho = ||r_bar_0||. The six features are exactly

$$
\mathbf f=
\left[
\rho-1,\;
\frac{\bar{\mathbf r}_0\cdot\bar{\mathbf v}_0}{\rho},\;
\|\bar{\mathbf v}_0\|^2-1,\;
\tau,\;
\frac{\bar z_0}{\rho},\;
\bar v_{z,0}
\right]. \tag{7}
$$

A 6 -> 48 -> 48 -> 48 -> 6 network uses tanh hidden activations and a linear output. Its parameter count is

$$
(6\cdot48+48)+2(48\cdot48+48)+(48\cdot6+6)=5334. \tag{8}
$$

Hidden weights use Xavier-normal initialization, biases are zero, and the last layer's weights/biases start at zero. Tanh provides smooth derivatives for AD; the choice is an engineering decision without a saved activation ablation.

The six outputs c_1,...,c_6 build corrections from the initial state and symmetry axis e_z:

$$
\mathbf c_r=c_1\bar{\mathbf r}_0+c_2\bar{\mathbf v}_0+c_3\mathbf e_z,\qquad
\mathbf c_v=c_4\bar{\mathbf r}_0+c_5\bar{\mathbf v}_0+c_6\mathbf e_z. \tag{9}
$$

These features and basis encode useful geometry of an axisymmetric force model. They do not establish universal representational sufficiency; near-degenerate state/basis cases deserve testing.

### 6.4 Hard initial conditions and Taylor trial solution

With a_bar_0 = a_bar(r_bar_0),

$$
\widehat{\bar{\mathbf r}}=
\bar{\mathbf r}_0+\tau\bar{\mathbf v}_0+
\tfrac12\tau^2\bar{\mathbf a}_0+\tau^3\mathbf c_r,
\qquad
\widehat{\bar{\mathbf v}}=
\bar{\mathbf v}_0+\tau\bar{\mathbf a}_0+\tau^2\mathbf c_v. \tag{10}
$$

At tau=0, r_hat=r_0 and v_hat=v_0 exactly. The derivatives also satisfy the initial kinematic/dynamic values. No soft initial-condition penalty is needed. The analytical trial captures lower-order motion while the network learns corrections.

Away from tau=0, position and velocity are separate outputs; their consistency is encouraged by the loss, not enforced identically by differentiating position.

### 6.5 Automatic-differentiation loss

$$
\mathcal R_r=\partial_\tau\widehat{\bar{\mathbf r}}-\widehat{\bar{\mathbf v}},
\qquad
\mathcal R_v=\partial_\tau\widehat{\bar{\mathbf v}}-
\bar{\mathbf a}(\widehat{\bar{\mathbf r}}). \tag{11}
$$

The actual objective is

$$
\mathcal L_{\rm PINN}=
\frac{1}{3B}\sum_{b=1}^{B}\left\|
\frac{\mathcal R_{r,b}}{\tau_b^2}\right\|^2+
\frac{1}{3B}\sum_{b=1}^{B}\left\|
\frac{\mathcal R_{v,b}}{\tau_b}\right\|^2. \tag{12}
$$

The component mean in code matters: each residual array has B x 3 entries. Dividing out small-time powers prevents a near-zero local time from trivially producing a small residual. Collocation tau is strictly positive; these divisions are not evaluated at zero.

Future SGP4 trajectories and ESA states are absent from this objective. Initial conditions are real GP-derived estimates; physics collocation points are equation constraints, not observed future samples. This is an ODE flow-map PINN, not a PDE field solver.

### 6.6 Actual training procedure

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Group split | Approximately 70/15/15% of unique exact element signatures |
| Main seed | 2026 |
| Segment | 60 s |
| Training collocation | Uniform local time in [0.02,1.0] x segment/T |
| Sampling | Initial states sampled with replacement |
| Fixed validation local times | [0.2,0.6,0.95] x segment/T, per validation state |
| Batch | 256 in the cited CPU runs |
| Arithmetic | float64 |
| Optimizer | Adam, initial learning rate 0.003 |
| Schedule | Cosine annealing to 0.00001 |
| Gradient norm clipping | 10 |
| Optimizer updates | 6,000 |
| Checkpoint selection | Minimum validation physics loss, inspected every 100 steps |
| Training log step zero | Initial diagnostic; not an optimizer update |

The schedule is

$$
\eta_s=\eta_{\min}+\tfrac12(\eta_0-\eta_{\min})
[1+\cos(\pi s/S)]. \tag{13}
$$

Adam uses moving gradient and squared-gradient estimates, bias correction, then updates theta using m_hat/(sqrt(v_hat)+epsilon). Unspecified Adam settings use the recorded PyTorch version's defaults; inspect that version if reporting their exact numeric values.

Why these choices: Adam is convenient for differentiable residual optimization; clipping limits large updates; cosine decay reduces the update size late in training; float64 assists numerical precision. No optimizer, precision, or architecture superiority claim is supported without ablations.

### 6.7 Rollout

$$
\widehat{\mathbf x}_{k+1}=\Phi_\theta(\widehat{\mathbf x}_k,\Delta t_k),
\qquad\widehat{\mathbf x}_0=\mathbf x_0. \tag{14}
$$

The trained short-time map is repeatedly applied. It is not directly trained on a three-hour time input. Rollout error includes accumulated local approximation, distribution shift of predicted states, approximate physics, and initial-state error.

## 7. Supervised SGP4 residual correction

This is a different network. Use **SGP4 + supervised neural residual correction** or **combined model**, not “SGP4 + physics-constrained PINN.”

### 7.1 RTN basis and targets

From each SGP4 state,

$$
\mathbf e_R=\mathbf r_S/\|\mathbf r_S\|,\quad
\mathbf e_N=\frac{\mathbf r_S\times\mathbf v_S}{\|\mathbf r_S\times\mathbf v_S\|},
\quad\mathbf e_T=\mathbf e_N\times\mathbf e_R,\quad
B_S=\begin{bmatrix}\mathbf e_R^\top\\\mathbf e_T^\top\\\mathbf e_N^\top\end{bmatrix}. \tag{15}
$$

Targets are

$$
\mathbf y(t)=
\begin{bmatrix}
B_S(\mathbf r_E-\mathbf r_S)\\
B_S(\mathbf v_E-\mathbf v_S)
\end{bmatrix}, \tag{16}
$$

where E denotes the aligned ESA reference.

Each component is scaled using training data only:

$$
s_j=\max\left(\sqrt{\frac1{N_{\rm tr}}\sum_{i\in{\rm tr}}y_{ij}^2},\epsilon_j\right),
\quad
\epsilon_{1:3}=0.001\ {\rm km},\quad
\epsilon_{4:6}=10^{-6}\ {\rm km/s}. \tag{17}
$$

### 7.2 Features, gate and prediction

With orbital period P, omega=2pi/P, and elapsed time in seconds,

$$
\mathbf h(t)=[\sin\omega t,\cos\omega t,\sin2\omega t,\cos2\omega t,t/5400],
\quad g(t)=1-\exp[-(t/60)^2]. \tag{18}
$$

P is 5921.061899469146 s in the primary saved run. Harmonics represent recurring orbital structure; elapsed time allows secular variation. Extrapolation is still empirical.

The 5 -> 32 -> 32 -> 6 tanh network has 1,446 parameters. Its output head starts at zero. Its normalized output is g(t)N_phi(h(t)). The correction vanishes at the common initial time:

$$
\boldsymbol\delta(t)=\mathbf s\odot g(t)N_\phi(\mathbf h(t)),\quad
\widehat{\mathbf r}_C=\mathbf r_S+B_S^\top\boldsymbol\delta_r,\quad
\widehat{\mathbf v}_C=\mathbf v_S+B_S^\top\boldsymbol\delta_v. \tag{19}
$$

The fit minimizes

$$
\mathcal L_{\rm correction}=
\frac1{6N_{\rm tr}}\sum_{i,j}
\left[g(t_i)N_{\phi,j}(\mathbf h(t_i))-y_{ij}/s_j\right]^2. \tag{20}
$$

Training uses full-batch AdamW, learning rate 0.003, weight decay 0.0001, 3,000 updates, clipping at 10, and the same cosine endpoint 0.00001. AdamW applies decoupled weight decay; it should not be mislabeled as an additional implemented physics penalty. Validation is checked every 100 steps.

Minutes 1–90 fit the network; 91–120 select the checkpoint; 121–180 are reserved for evaluation. Inference requires SGP4 states/time and saved configuration, with no ESA test state as input.

Separate position/velocity corrections do not guarantee d(r_C)/dt=v_C, conservation, or force consistency. The combined model is calibrated for this Sentinel-1D GP arc, not trained as a transferable debris-catalog corrector.

## 8. Continuous-interval conjunction screening

### 8.1 Why a sampled-distance test is insufficient

Fast-moving objects can pass within the threshold between two sample times while remaining far apart at both endpoints. The implementation searches swept interval chords before direct-model refinement.

For one interval of duration h, object i has endpoints p_i^0,p_i^1:

$$
\mathbf m_i=(\mathbf p_i^0+\mathbf p_i^1)/2,\quad
\ell_i=\|\mathbf p_i^1-\mathbf p_i^0\|/2,\quad
p_A=Ah^2/8,\quad b_i=\ell_i+p_A. \tag{21}
$$

A cKDTree query proposes midpoint pairs within 2 max_i(b_i)+d_thr; each proposal is filtered by its own b_i+b_j+d_thr.

A=0.05 km/s^2 is an assumed acceleration bound. At h=60 s, the per-object padding is 22.5 km. Padding is an interpolation allowance, not a covariance or measured forecast uncertainty.

### 8.2 Linear relative minimum

$$
\mathbf q_0=\mathbf p_i^0-\mathbf p_j^0,\quad
\Delta\mathbf q=(\mathbf p_i^1-\mathbf p_i^0)-(\mathbf p_j^1-\mathbf p_j^0),
$$

$$
u^*=\operatorname{clip}_{[0,1]}
\left(-\frac{\mathbf q_0^\top\Delta\mathbf q}{\|\Delta\mathbf q\|^2}\right),
\quad d_{\rm linear}=\|\mathbf q_0+u^*\Delta\mathbf q\|. \tag{22}
$$

Zero/negligible relative displacement uses u*=0. Keep pairs with d_linear <= d_thr+2p_A.

### 8.3 Direct refinement and event aggregation

- SGP4: bounded minimization of squared direct-SGP4 separation on each candidate interval; explicitly compare both endpoints. Numerical x tolerance is 0.001 s, maximum 80 iterations.
- PINN: direct local-map separation from the interval's neural initial states, batched golden-section search with 27 iterations, plus endpoint comparison.
- Merge consecutive candidate intervals into episodes and report the smallest refined separation per episode when within threshold.
- Preserve failed refinements, excluded states, unresolved shared-orbit pairs, and rejected candidates.

Relative speed is ||v_i(t_CA)-v_j(t_CA)||. Shared identical-element pairs cannot yield independently resolved physical separation.

Local minimization and an assumed acceleration bound do not prove exhaustive detection, particularly for pathological neural curves or persistent co-orbiting objects. Step-size and brute-force convergence studies are needed.

### 8.4 Complexity

Naive sampling is O(KN^2). The broad phase typically costs approximately O(KN log N + C), with C output/candidate work; dense queries can still approach quadratic cost. Refinement adds O(C_ref I C_state). PINN rollout is approximately O(KNP_theta), treating network parameter count as a dense-evaluation proxy. Stored full trajectories require O(NK) memory. These are algorithmic descriptions, not demonstrated universal performance guarantees.

## 9. Optional collision probability

Current GP inputs lack encounter covariance and justified object radii. Current reported probabilities therefore remain null. The optional implementation exists but has not established calibrated operational probabilities.

Assuming independent Gaussian position errors at the encounter,

$$
C_{\rm rel}=C_1+C_2,\quad
\mathbf n=\mathbf v_{\rm rel}/\|\mathbf v_{\rm rel}\|,\quad
\mathbf m=E(\mathbf r_1-\mathbf r_2),\quad
\Sigma=EC_{\rm rel}E^\top, \tag{23}
$$

where E has two orthonormal rows spanning the plane perpendicular to n. With correlated objects the general covariance would include -C_12-C_21; that option is not implemented.

For supplied combined hard-body radius R_H,

$$
P_c=\int_{x^2+y^2\le R_H^2}
\frac{\exp[-\tfrac12(\mathbf z-\mathbf m)^\top\Sigma^{-1}(\mathbf z-\mathbf m)]}
{2\pi\sqrt{\det\Sigma}}\,d\mathbf z. \tag{24}
$$

The code reduces this to a one-dimensional integral using the conditional normal distribution:

$$
\mu_{y|x}=m_y+\frac{\Sigma_{yx}}{\Sigma_{xx}}(x-m_x),\qquad
\sigma_{y|x}^2=\Sigma_{yy}-\frac{\Sigma_{yx}^2}{\Sigma_{xx}}, \tag{25}
$$

$$
P_c=\int_{-R_H}^{R_H} f_X(x)
\left[
\Phi\!\left(\frac{\sqrt{R_H^2-x^2}-\mu_{y|x}}{\sigma_{y|x}}\right)
-\Phi\!\left(\frac{-\sqrt{R_H^2-x^2}-\mu_{y|x}}{\sigma_{y|x}}\right)
\right]dx. \tag{26}
$$

Implementation standardizes x, clips its integration range to +/-12 standard deviations, and uses scipy quad with absolute tolerance 10^-12, relative tolerance 10^-7, limit 200. These are numerical settings, not uncertainty validation; the returned quadrature-error estimate is not retained in the result.

Inputs must identify the pair and TCA within one second, TEME frame, km/km^2 units, symmetric positive-semidefinite 3x3 object covariances, positive radius, independence assumption and provenance. The projected 2D covariance must be positive definite. Relative speeds below 0.01 km/s are rejected.

Assumptions include a short approximately rectilinear encounter, Gaussian uncertainty and valid physical sizes. The procedure does not propagate covariance or automatically incorporate PINN error. Background: [NASA close-approach risk assessment](https://www.nasa.gov/cara/step-2-close-approach-risk-assessment/).

## 10. Evaluation formulas

### 10.1 Regression

For N scored states, with e_i = r_hat_i-r_ref_i,

$$
{\rm RMSE}_{r}=\sqrt{\frac1N\sum_i\|\mathbf e_i\|^2},\quad
{\rm MAE}_{r}=\frac1N\sum_i\|\mathbf e_i\|,\quad
{\rm bias}_j=\frac1N\sum_i e_{ij}. \tag{27}
$$

$$
{\rm RMSE}_j=\sqrt{\frac1N\sum_i e_{ij}^2},\qquad
{\rm MAE}_j=\frac1N\sum_i|e_{ij}|. \tag{28}
$$

Velocity metrics use the same definitions with velocity errors. Position/velocity p95 is the 0.95 quantile of vector norms; maximum and final-time errors are separately reported. Vector MAE is mean Euclidean norm, not the average of three component absolute errors. Vector RMSE is sqrt(sum_j RMSE_j^2).

RTN error uses B_ref e at each time. Catalog comparisons use the SGP4 reference basis; ESA comparisons use the ESA basis. Corrector training uses the SGP4 basis. These choices must not be silently interchanged. Velocity RTN error is projected inertial velocity error, not a derivative in the rotating RTN frame.

The common initial state is excluded from aggregate scores. In split metrics, the preceding interval boundary is included in an array for diagnostics and then excluded by orbit_error_metrics. Thus the primary test scores exactly indices 121–180, not 120–180. The field initial_position_error_km in that test block refers to the preceding boundary, not the global t0.

Relative improvement for a lower-is-better error is

$$
100(1-E_{\rm new}/E_{\rm baseline})\%. \tag{29}
$$

It is an error reduction, not a collision-accuracy percentage.

### 10.2 Pair classification

For M eligible objects and S unresolved shared pairs,

$$
N_{\rm pairs}=M(M-1)/2-S. \tag{30}
$$

TP, FP, FN and TN refer to pair flags within the same window/threshold:

$$
{\rm Accuracy}=\frac{TP+TN}{TP+TN+FP+FN},\quad
{\rm Precision}=\frac{TP}{TP+FP},\quad
{\rm Recall}=\frac{TP}{TP+FN},
$$

$$
F_1=\frac{2TP}{2TP+FP+FN},\quad
{\rm Specificity}=\frac{TN}{TN+FP},\quad
{\rm BalancedAccuracy}=\tfrac12({\rm Recall}+{\rm Specificity}),
$$

$$
{\rm NPV}=\frac{TN}{TN+FN},\quad
{\rm FPR}=\frac{FP}{FP+TN},\quad
{\rm FNR}=\frac{FN}{FN+TP},
$$

$$
{\rm MCC}=\frac{TP\,TN-FP\,FN}
{\sqrt{(TP+FP)(TP+FN)(TN+FP)(TN+FN)}}. \tag{31}
$$

A zero denominator means undefined/null, not zero or perfect performance. Test-only pair metrics require both objects to be held out. SGP4-reference labels measure agreement; supplied independent labels measure only their audited labeled subset.

ROC AUC integrates TPR over FPR across score thresholds; PR AUC integrates precision over recall with a specified integration convention. Brier score is N^-1 sum_i(p_i-y_i)^2. These are definitions for future evaluation, not currently available results: suitable independent labels and meaningful scores are missing. A hard distance flag is not a calibrated collision probability.

### 10.3 Episode matching

The dedicated catalog comparison groups events by unordered pair and uses linear_sum_assignment to maximize valid one-to-one matches within 120 s, then minimize absolute time difference. Invalid assignments receive a penalty larger than the total valid-assignment cost. Matched/unmatched counts yield event precision, recall and F1; no episode true-negative universe is defined.

For matched events, signed time and distance errors are t_PINN-t_SGP4 and d_PINN-d_SGP4. MAE, RMSE and maximum absolute differences are saved. Do not interpret the older standalone run's pair-oriented event comparison as the same one-to-one protocol without checking its source.

### 10.4 Physical consistency

With P2(u)=(3u^2-1)/2,

$$
U=-\frac{\mu}{r}\left[1-J_2(R_E/r)^2P_2(z/r)\right],\quad
{\cal E}=\tfrac12\|\mathbf v\|^2+U,\quad
h_z=(\mathbf r\times\mathbf v)_z. \tag{32}
$$

Diagnostics include |(E(t)-E(0))/E(0)|, |h_z(t)-h_z(0)|, and finite-difference residuals

$$
D_t\mathbf r-\mathbf v,\qquad D_t\mathbf v-\mathbf a(\mathbf r). \tag{33}
$$

Their vector RMS is sqrt(mean_i ||residual_i||^2), unlike the component means in the training loss. The implementation uses interior finite differences for residual summaries; discretization affects values. Central/J2 consistency does not rank observational accuracy across models with different forces. Full angular momentum is not generally conserved under J2; the axial component is the relevant invariant here.

### 10.5 Runtime

Report training, prediction, screening and I/O separately. Three-model prediction timing is the median of five warmed measurements with rotated model order; combined timing includes SGP4. Catalog prediction measurements alternate order. CPU wall time can vary with load and scheduling. A smaller screening runtime can reflect less diagnostic work, not a better propagator.

## 12. Interpretation and threats to validity

1. **Reference distinction:** SGP4 agreement, ESA regression and independent event detection answer different questions.
2. **Unequal information:** only the combined method sees earlier ESA residuals. Its improvement cannot isolate architecture superiority.
3. **Limited external validation:** one Sentinel satellite and overlapping short arcs do not represent debris populations.
4. **Dependence:** timestamps are autocorrelated; exact-orbit grouping does not remove breakup-family dependence.
5. **Physics mismatch:** the PINN's simplified force model and rollout can accumulate substantial along-track error.
6. **Initial error:** a common GP-derived state already differs from ESA by about 451 m.
7. **Reference/frame uncertainty:** RESORB, predicted Earth orientation and terrestrial realization are not error-free.
8. **Retrospective timing:** later-downloaded products do not establish a live forecast.
9. **Class imbalance:** millions of negative pairs can create near-perfect accuracy with missed encounters.
10. **Small positive test support:** one positive held-out pair cannot support broad detection claims.
11. **Screening approximation:** numerical tolerance is not physical accuracy; completeness is not proven.
12. **Runtime variability:** one machine and process timings do not establish hardware-general scaling.
13. **Repeated test exposure:** the saved configuration says the method was locked before evaluation; future tuning on these published test results requires a new untouched test set.
14. **Publication novelty:** no exhaustive orbital-PINN or hybrid-propagation literature review has been completed here.

A balanced conclusion is that the system provides a reproducible experimental framework and a limited promising residual-calibration result, while standalone PINN errors and evidence gaps constrain collision-screening claims.

## 13. Experiments needed before stronger claims

These are proposed experiments, not completed results.

| Priority | Experiment | Purpose / required output |
|---|---|---|
| Essential | Multi-object, multi-date independent orbit evaluation | Distribution of per-arc errors, coverage and outliers |
| Essential | Same-force numerical integrator baseline, e.g. well-converged RK/DOP853 | Separate learning error from omitted physics |
| Essential | Equal-information correction baselines: bias, linear trend, harmonic least squares, regularized regression | Test whether a neural network adds value |
| Essential | Multiple predefined seeds and untouched outer test arcs | Quantify training variability and avoid selection leakage |
| Essential | Horizon sweep and 10/30/60-second rollout/screening convergence | Identify accumulated error and missed-minimum sensitivity |
| Essential for collision claims | Independent encounter labels with explicit negatives | Measure event/pair detection beyond SGP4 agreement |
| Essential for probability claims | Audited covariance, sizes, calibration and outcome validation | Establish justified probabilistic risk |
| High | With/without J2; scaled/unscaled loss; trial/vanilla model; trained/untrained | Isolate each proposed methodological contribution |
| High | Family-, object- and date-held-out evaluation | Test generalization beyond exact-signature grouping |
| High | Dense-force reference and perturbation ablations | Measure impact of drag, higher harmonics and maneuvers |
| High | Corrector kinematic/physics constraints | Test whether accuracy gains coexist with consistent dynamics |
| High | Calibration-length, harmonic-feature, gate and regularization ablations | Establish sensitivity of the combined method |
| High | Equal diagnostic workloads and scaling curves | Fair end-to-end runtime comparison |
| Supporting | Failure and largest-error case studies | Explain operationally relevant limitations |

For repeated experiments, report paired per-arc differences, mean/median, dispersion, seed counts and confidence intervals. Bootstrap independent satellites/arcs or justified temporal blocks; do not treat 60 correlated timestamps as 60 independent experiments. With too few independent arcs, report descriptive evidence instead of manufacturing significance.

Example future estimand: mean over independent arcs of RMSE_corrected minus RMSE_baseline. Freeze hyperparameters using training/validation arcs before an outer test. An improvement across one arc is not a significance test.

## 15. Paper writing blueprint

### 15.1 Suggested abstract draft

*This study evaluates physics-informed short-time orbital propagation and supervised residual correction for reproducible conjunction-screening research. A neural flow map enforces initial conditions through a Taylor trial solution and is trained on central-gravity and J2 differential-equation residuals using catalog-derived initial states. A shared-input experiment over 1,980 objects compares the resulting trajectories and screening decisions with SGP4, while a separate Sentinel-1D benchmark uses frame-aligned ESA restituted orbit states. In the catalog experiment, the PINN attains a held-out position RMSE of 2.095 km relative to SGP4 and pair-level precision and recall of 0.938 and 0.882. On a reserved 60-state interval of a three-hour independent-reference experiment, position RMSE is 503.486 m for SGP4, 3715.756 m for the standalone PINN, and 275.348 m for SGP4 with a supervised neural correction. The correction uses earlier reference observations unavailable to the standalone baselines. These results demonstrate a replayable evaluation framework and a limited retrospective calibration benefit, while highlighting accumulated neural propagation error and the need for broader independent validation. No observational collision-detection accuracy or calibrated collision probability is established.*

Adapt abstract length and structure to the selected venue. Do not add “significant,” “real-time,” or “state-of-the-art” without supporting experiments.

Suggested keywords: physics-informed neural networks; orbital propagation; SGP4; space debris; conjunction screening; residual learning; independent orbit validation.

### 15.2 Section-by-section manuscript plan

| Manuscript section | Content and evidence |
|---|---|
| Introduction | Practical orbital screening problem, limitations of GP/uncertainty, explicit research questions |
| Related work | SGP4, numerical propagation, orbital scientific ML, residual correction, conjunction validation |
| Problem and data | Equations (1)–(4), selected catalog, reference product, provenance and leakage controls |
| Methods | Equations (5)–(26), exact PINN/corrector distinction, screening pseudocode |
| Experimental design | Object and chronological splits, information budgets, baselines, timing and metrics |
| Results | Separate catalog agreement, frozen one-hour benchmark and calibrated three-model results |
| Discussion | Error growth, outliers, unequal information, computation, physical consistency |
| Limitations | Section 12, including retrospective products and unavailable collision metrics |
| Conclusion | Evidence-supported findings, scope and specific next experiments |
| Data/code availability | Archive location, version/commit or hashes, weights, configs and licensing |
| Declarations | Actual authorship, contributions, funding, conflicts and applicable disclosures |
| Appendices/supplement | Full hyperparameters, formulas, supplementary metrics and reproducibility artifacts |

Do not fabricate author names, affiliations, funding, ethics approvals, conflicts or repository DOI. Fill these from the actual research team and archive.

### 15.3 Paper-ready algorithm descriptions

~~~text
Algorithm 1: Physics-trained local orbital flow map
Input: validated GP initial states, grouped splits, seed, segment h
1. Normalize initial positions and velocities.
2. Initialize the Taylor-correction network with a zero output head.
3. Sample training initial states and strictly positive local times.
4. Evaluate trial states and automatic-differentiation residuals.
5. Minimize scaled kinematic + dynamic residual mean squares.
6. Select weights using fixed validation collocation states/times.
7. Freeze weights and roll out the local map over the forecast grid.
8. Evaluate future trajectories only after selection.
Output: frozen checkpoint, trajectories, actual training/audit records.
~~~

~~~text
Algorithm 2: Shared interval screening
Input: model states on a grid, threshold, acceleration-padding assumption
1. Remove invalid/stale objects and unresolved identical-orbit pairs.
2. Build swept-chord midpoint bounds for each interval.
3. Query a spatial tree and reject pairs using linear relative minima.
4. Refine surviving intervals with the corresponding direct model.
5. Include endpoints; aggregate consecutive candidate intervals.
6. Save accepted episodes, rejected candidates and refinement failures.
Output: model-based encounters, never assumed collision probabilities.
~~~

~~~text
Algorithm 3: Chronological residual correction
Input: SGP4 trajectory, aligned early ESA states, fixed split boundaries
1. Construct SGP4 RTN residual targets for training/validation only.
2. Compute component scales from the training subset only.
3. Train the gated harmonic-feature correction with AdamW.
4. Select the checkpoint using validation residual loss.
5. Freeze weights; infer the reserved interval using SGP4/time only.
6. Compare all model states against the same reserved ESA timestamps.
Output: corrected trajectories and split-specific independent errors.
~~~

Web references checked during preparation on 20 September 2026. Confirm publication metadata and current target-venue requirements before submission.

For the final literature review, build a comparison matrix covering orbital PINNs, neural integrators, SGP4 residual correction, physics/data hybrids, uncertainty calibration and conjunction screening. For each paper record forces, inputs, number of satellites/arcs, held-out design, external reference, baselines, errors and runtime. Distinguish a method's claimed novelty from independently verified comparative evidence. Add recent primary research only after reading it.

IEEE formatting uses the chosen publication's template. Springer journal and proceedings requirements differ; follow the selected venue's author instructions. Formatting alone does not establish research quality.

## 18. Submission checklist

- [ ] Select a specific journal or conference and verify its current template and scope.
- [ ] Finish a primary-source related-work comparison before making novelty claims.
- [ ] Clearly distinguish standalone PINN from supervised neural correction.
- [ ] Identify reference, frame, units, horizon and split for every metric.
- [ ] Preserve unequal-information and retrospective-study disclosures.
- [ ] Include unfavorable PINN errors, outliers and slower runtime.
- [ ] Complete independent multi-arc validation and fair baseline/ablation studies.
- [ ] Report uncertainty using independent experimental units.
- [ ] Never label SGP4 agreement as observed collision accuracy.
- [ ] Keep unavailable collision probabilities and classification scores unavailable.
- [ ] Check all tables against numeric artifacts and all equations against code.
- [ ] Archive code, inputs where redistribution permits, weights and environment.
- [ ] Document actual author contributions, funding, conflicts and required disclosures.
- [ ] Ensure figure captions, references and supplementary materials are complete.

### 19.5 Coverage statement

This document indexes 38 archived runs and embeds 42 original metric JSON files. All run status files are included. Failed runs remain marked failed. Per-time, per-object and per-encounter data, full source snapshots and neural weights are linked rather than converted into Markdown. The 19-section main text derives the implemented project-level equations; the complete SGP4 theory remains in the cited original reference and the pinned implementation. Additional experiments in Section 13 and the unfinished literature review are explicitly proposals, not saved outcomes.
